title: Comparison: Legislative Assembly vs Legislative Council

blocks.content: The Legislative Council is a permanent body and not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every second year.

rows: Permanent body (1/3rd members retire every 2 years)
Exclusive authority to introduce and pass
Can only delay up to 14 days, cannot reject or amend

items: The Legislative Council can delay an Ordinary Bill for a maximum period of 4 months total (3 months in the first instance and 1 month in the second instance).
Only 6 states currently have bicameral legislatures in India: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.
There is no constitutional provision for a joint sitting at the state level to resolve legislative deadlocks between the Assembly and the Council.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) is the directly elected lower house, while the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is the indirectly elected upper house.
The Legislative Assembly has a 5-year term subject to dissolution, whereas the Legislative Council is a permanent body where one-third of members retire every two years.
Money Bills can only originate in the Legislative Assembly, and the Legislative Council can delay a Money Bill for a maximum of 14 days only.
Under Article 169, Parliament can create or abolish a Legislative Council if the state's Legislative Assembly passes a resolution by a special majority.
Unlike Parliament at the central level, there is no provision for a joint sitting of both state houses to resolve deadlocks on legislative bills.
